page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration built on the arm64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent compute performance without resource sharing or core oversubscription.

A key component of this instance profile is its bundled local storage, consisting of a single 403 GB local NVMe solid-state drive. The instance contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default, necessitating external network configuration if direct internet ingress is required.

By coupling an energy-efficient Arm processor architecture with direct-attached NVMe storage, the instance delivers high I/O density and strong operational cost efficiency for workloads that demand rapid disk throughput. However, because local NVMe SSD storage is ephemeral, deployments requiring durability must replicate data to persistent storage. The configuration is appropriate for distributed cache nodes, database read replicas, continuous integration build environments, and containerized microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the 64-bit Arm architecture, offering 4 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16 GB of system RAM. With a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration maintains a balanced hardware profile suitable for diverse operational requirements. A prominent hardware feature is the inclusion of a bundled 403 GB local NVMe SSD, providing high-speed ephemeral storage directly to the host without relying purely on network-attached disks. The instance features no discrete graphics processing units and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Providing dedicated CPU cores alongside fast local NVMe storage yields efficient performance per resource for I/O-intensive services. This virtual server is appropriate for database caching, build and deployment systems, containerized web applications, and intermediate data processing pipelines requiring fast local scratch storage.
